computation_model.label: Classical bit-RAM · v1
computation_model.preprocessing: Single target; all attack setup charged. No amortization or target-specific advice.
computation_model.memory: Unbounded capacity; each indirect one-bit read/write costs one operation. Peak storage is reported separately.
semantics: One Boolean operation of at most two bit-register inputs costs one; fixed wiring, constants and bit permutations are free.
Indirect reads and writes cost one per transferred bit, independently of memory size. Address construction is additional work.
Register layouts and executable program are fixed by the public configuration, never by an unknown target answer.
Integer/field arithmetic, comparisons, branches and hashes are expanded into the declared elementary algorithms.
Every reported cost is a conservative work budget, not expected Python runtime or a lower bound on all attacks.

models.label: Interval baby-step–giant-step
models.scope: Complete shared-key recovery on this exact release; at least 50% success under the note's scoped premises.
limitations: Research baseline with deliberately elementary arithmetic. Not best-known attack cost or a security lower bound.

estimates.label: Interval baby-step–giant-step
estimates.human: Baby-step–giant-step searches the actual published exponent interval. It recovers the recipient exponent, computes the shared group element, and applies the scheme's exact transcript hash. The displayed work is a conservative upper bound with success one for honest inputs. No random-walk assumption is needed. The large table is explicitly included. This is a reproducible baseline, not the cheapest known finite-field attack; number-field-sieve and reusable-precomputation improvements are absent.
estimates.technical:
Write every candidate x in [0,M] uniquely as x=im+j, with m=ceil(sqrt(M+1)), 0<=j<m and 0<=i<ceil((M+1)/m). Store (g^j,j), or (jG,j) for a curve, in a bottom-up mergesorted table. A giant-step lookup compares the target times g^(-im), or target-imG, against the table. Equality yields x; check x<=M and verify the public key. No probabilistic collision model or constant-time hash-table premise is used. The table has distinct group elements because m<=q. Binary search uses at most ceil(log2(m))+1 comparisons. Sorting uses at most m*ceil(log2(m)) comparisons and twice that many record transfers. Each comparison reads both full records and pays a bitwise comparison plus address/control work. Two table arrays are reserved in the memory bound. Records occupy padded power-of-two bit slots. Each bit address concatenates the record index with a fixed, unrolled offset; this avoids treating a variable address multiplication or an entire RAM word transfer as free. All padding is included in the storage bound. Eight counter-update/compare allowances per table control step cover the input/output pointers and branches. Here M=99256, m=316, giant iterations=315, key width=32, record width=41 bits. All quantities are exact integers until the final log2 display. The work bound covers success probability one, hence also the shared 50% target. This does not assert the budget is minimal for achieving that target.

For this release the public certificates prove prime p,q and ord(g)=q; the honest x,r lie in [1,M] with M<q. Thus there is a unique x in that interval. The recovered x gives c^x=g^(rx). The final SHA-256 input has 106 bytes including all uint32 framing, profile, p,q,g, X,C,Z. No hash collision-resistance hypothesis is needed to compute the same hash. The profile-specific public constants are part of the input specification; all baby-table preparation is charged again for each target.

estimates.label: Trial-division recovery baseline
estimates.human: This deliberately elementary baseline tries every odd candidate for the smaller certified RSA factor, reconstructs the private exponent, and recovers the encapsulated integer and transcript hash. It is guaranteed on honest inputs. It is substantially slower than established factoring attacks, including Pollard rho and the number field sieve. A high point on this curve is therefore not evidence of strong RSA security. Its purpose is to provide a complete, reproducible RAM accounting baseline until better factoring analyses have been admitted under the same model.
estimates.technical: For an n-bit modulus the adapter samples a factor q of exactly k=floor(n/2) bits. All such factors are odd. Try every d=2^(k-1)+1,2^(k-1)+3,...,2^k-1. There are exactly 2^(k-2)=16384 candidates. Restoring binary division finds q (or another prime factor) with certainty, independent of the nonuniform Pocklington sampler. Set p=N/q and phi=(p-1)(q-1). To avoid an unaccounted large-integer inverse, exploit the fixed prime e=65537: set u=(phi mod e)^(e-2) mod e and t=(-u) mod e. Then d=(1+t*phi)/e is an integer with ed=1 mod phi and d<phi. The sampler enforces gcd(e,phi)=1. Compute z=c^d mod N, including z that is not a unit; Fermat and CRT prove recovery for every honest z. Verify z^e=c, then apply the exact framed 82-byte SHA-256 transcript. All primitive costs and loop control are charged; O(n) workspace suffices. This upper bound is neither a best-known factoring estimate nor a hardness premise.

models.label: Curve baby-step–giant-step

sources.title: Menezes, van Oorschot and Vanstone, Handbook of Applied Cryptography, Chapter 3: discrete logarithms and factoring
Handbook of Applied Cryptography, Chapter 14: integer and modular arithmetic

estimates.label: Curve baby-step–giant-step
estimates.human: Baby-step–giant-step recovers the scalar of the public point on the exact registered curve, then reconstructs the shared point and transcript hash. The work bound includes point decoding, affine field arithmetic, sorting, table lookup and hashing. It succeeds for every honest input without a random-walk premise. Its table is large, and its elementary affine arithmetic is intentionally unoptimized. This is an attainable-work baseline, not a claim that every attack is this expensive.
estimates.technical:
Write every candidate x in [0,M] uniquely as x=im+j, with m=ceil(sqrt(M+1)), 0<=j<m and 0<=i<ceil((M+1)/m). Store (g^j,j), or (jG,j) for a curve, in a bottom-up mergesorted table. A giant-step lookup compares the target times g^(-im), or target-imG, against the table. Equality yields x; check x<=M and verify the public key. No probabilistic collision model or constant-time hash-table premise is used. The table has distinct group elements because m<=q. Binary search uses at most ceil(log2(m))+1 comparisons. Sorting uses at most m*ceil(log2(m)) comparisons and twice that many record transfers. Each comparison reads both full records and pays a bitwise comparison plus address/control work. Two table arrays are reserved in the memory bound. Records occupy padded power-of-two bit slots. Each bit address concatenates the record index with a fixed, unrolled offset; this avoids treating a variable address multiplication or an entire RAM word transfer as free. All padding is included in the storage bound. Eight counter-update/compare allowances per table control step cover the input/output pointers and branches. Here M=79186, m=282, giant iterations=281, key width=35, record width=44 bits. All quantities are exact integers until the final log2 display. The work bound covers success probability one, hence also the shared 50% target. This does not assert the budget is minimal for achieving that target.

The published prime/order certificates establish that G has prime order q and the entire nonsingular curve has order q. Table keys retain both affine coordinates and an infinity flag, so x-coordinate sign collisions are not discarded. All denominators in nonexceptional additions are invertible; identity, equality and opposite-point branches are handled explicitly. Use inversion z^(p-2), charged by binary exponentiation, and the usual affine formulas. Each group addition is bounded by one inversion, six modular products and twenty linear-width operations. Two compressed points are decoded using the actual p=3 mod4 rule. Then xC=rX and the same 150-byte framed input produces the same SHA-256 output. The curve's canonical public JSON is a fixed public profile constant. No unproved curve-hardness or hash-hardness premise is used by this attack.

sources.title: FIPS 203, Algorithms 14 and 17: deterministic ML-KEM encapsulation

estimates.label: Native-message enumeration
estimates.human: Try every 8-bit native message, re-create its complete ciphertext, and derive the shared key from the matching message. The plot counts the actual transform and polynomial work as bit operations. Faster lattice or structural attacks are outside this baseline.
estimates.technical:
### Why enumeration recovers the complete shared secret

Fix an honest key and any public encapsulation salt. Let F(x) be the deterministic
ciphertext produced by native input x and K(x) its derived key. Enumerate every
input and return K(x) for the first exact full-ciphertext match. This algorithm
does not receive a correctness oracle or the challenge target key.

Suppose an honest PKE decoder D fails to return x on at most a fraction delta of
uniform native inputs. The good inputs are injective under F: D(F(x)) cannot
equal two different x. A first-match attack can be wrong on at most all bad
inputs, plus one good input for each bad first representative. There are at most
as many such good inputs as bad inputs. Hence its key-recovery success is at
least 1-2*delta. The statement also holds after averaging over keys and salts.
It uses message recovery, not merely agreement of KEM outputs. No hash collision
resistance or random-oracle premise is needed for this combinatorial lemma.

This is a full-space, worst-case work budget that achieves at least 1/2 success;
it is not the minimum possible budget for 1/2 success. Early stopping only saves
work. Where every input decodes, success is exactly one in the mathematical
implementation. Operational faults are not a cryptanalytic assumption.

### Exact module account
Use q=3329, n=8, rank2, CBD3/CBD2, du10/dv4. Cache public A and H(pk), then run the documented NTT program for all 2^8 messages. A butterfly has one modular product and two modular additions; each quadratic NTT base product uses five modular products and two additions. Count two forward transforms, three inverse transforms and six polynomial base products per message. Compress all 3n coefficients via bounded-width integer division. G and all five noise XOF calls use the exact parameter/purpose domains. Compare all ciphertext bits and output the 32-byte K already produced by G. The matrix expansion uses a deliberately conservative 65536-byte bound per polynomial. The exact registered key generator, including its degree256 endpoint, calls the same capped SampleNTT routine; its maximum successful prefix is49152 bytes. Thus every issued public key has its matrix reproduced within this bound. This argument concerns successful generation by the registered release and does not claim a finite worst-case cap for arbitrary uncapped FIPS203 key generation. Arithmetic and control counts are upper bounds for this specified program, not operation timings of CPython.

### Memory layout and control conventions

Polynomial and matrix scalar slots and matrix row strides are padded to powers
of two. An indexed slot address is the concatenation of the public-width index
and a fixed intra-slot bit offset; bit transfers inside a scalar are unrolled.
The storage bound includes that padding. Loop/control allowances cover up to
eight counter increment/comparison pairs per compound step. Arithmetic
subroutines use the common register-level bounds; array reads/writes are charged
separately. The fixed13-entry Frodo CDF scan is unrolled. None of these costs
are measured CPython instruction counts. The bounds specify an elementary
implementation; they are deliberately less optimized than production kernels.

assumptions.title: At most one eighth of honest messages fail to decode
assumptions.human: For the actual seeded scheme, require \(\Pr[D(F(m))\ne m]\le 1/8\). This is enough for the enumeration attack to recover the key with probability at least \(3/4\). The transfer from the idealized correctness analysis remains unproved.
assumptions.technical: The assumed event concerns the real fixed SHA3/SHAKE implementation, averaged over its stated key/message distribution: Pr[D(F(m)) != m] <= 1/8. It is a message-decoding statement, not just KEM key agreement; literal information-theoretic independence of long expansions from fixed finite seeds is not asserted.

### Bounded-column recovery and success proof

Enumerate every s in {-12,...,12}^n separately for each of the eight columns of
B. Retain the first vector whose residual b-A*s, centered modulo 32768, lies
in {-12,...,12}^n. The actual secret column always passes. The finite sampler's
support is a fact of the specified CDF, not a Gaussian approximation.

Condition on the true S,E and assume A is an independent uniform matrix over
Z/(2^15). For a false candidate, d=s-s_true is nonzero with coordinates bounded
by24. Its coordinate gcd with2^15 is2^v with v<=4. For one uniform row of A,

at most ceil(25/2^v) lie in this subgroup. For v=0,...,4 the probability is at

columns and at most25^n-1 false vectors gives 8(25^n-1)2^(-10n). No independence
between candidate events or between the eight columns is asserted or needed.

most1/8. Combined with the separate actual message-decoding premise delta<=1/8,
this gives success at least3/4. At n=8 decoding is perfect and the bound is7/8.
Early matches can only save work; the budget scans all25^n vectors per column.

tail probabilities into the actual seeded distribution without a new argument.

estimates.label: Native-message enumeration

assumptions.title: At most one eighth of honest messages fail to decode
assumptions.human: For the actual seeded scheme, require \(\Pr[D(F(m))\ne m]\le 1/8\). The ideal-noise correctness analysis supports this conservative threshold, but its transfer to fixed SHAKE remains a premise.
assumptions.technical: Assume the actual seeded key/message/salt distribution has message-decoding failure probability at most1/8. The local exact rational Chernoff/union certificate bounds the64 residuals E''+sum(S'E−E'S), with threshold4096, by2^-133 under independent finite-CDF noise. That stronger ideal-model statement motivates, but does not prove, the weaker actual-event bound used here. No literal independence of a long deterministic SHAKE expansion is claimed.

estimates.human: Try every 128-bit native message while keeping the observed public salt fixed; reproduce the full ciphertext and final shared key. The nearly flat ceiling comes from the real fixed message space. It is not evidence that lattice attacks are equally expensive.
estimates.technical:
### Why enumeration recovers the complete shared secret

Fix an honest key and any public encapsulation salt. Let F(x) be the deterministic
ciphertext produced by native input x and K(x) its derived key. Enumerate every
input and return K(x) for the first exact full-ciphertext match. This algorithm
does not receive a correctness oracle or the challenge target key.

Suppose an honest PKE decoder D fails to return x on at most a fraction delta of
uniform native inputs. The good inputs are injective under F: D(F(x)) cannot
equal two different x. A first-match attack can be wrong on at most all bad
inputs, plus one good input for each bad first representative. There are at most
as many such good inputs as bad inputs. Hence its key-recovery success is at
least 1-2*delta. The statement also holds after averaging over keys and salts.
It uses message recovery, not merely agreement of KEM outputs. No hash collision
resistance or random-oracle premise is needed for this combinatorial lemma.

This is a full-space, worst-case work budget that achieves at least 1/2 success;
it is not the minimum possible budget for 1/2 success. Early stopping only saves
work. Where every input decodes, success is exactly one in the mathematical
implementation. Operational faults are not a cryptanalytic assumption.

### Exact salted Frodo account
For n=192, q=32768 and nbar8, precompute all n public SHAKE128 rows and H(pk). For each of 2^128 messages use the observed 32-byte ciphertext salt. Expand 16n+64 noise values; a linear scan of the 13 CDF thresholds reproduces bisect_left exactly. Compute S'A and S'B with 8n²+64n modular multiply-adds. Encode, compare the entire ciphertext including its salt, and compute SHAKE128(ct||k,16). Native message search does not guess the public salt and does not truncate any seed. Final shared-key hashing is charged for every candidate, a conservative overhead.

### Memory layout and control conventions

Polynomial and matrix scalar slots and matrix row strides are padded to powers
of two. An indexed slot address is the concatenation of the public-width index
and a fixed intra-slot bit offset; bit transfers inside a scalar are unrolled.
The storage bound includes that padding. Loop/control allowances cover up to
eight counter increment/comparison pairs per compound step. Arithmetic
subroutines use the common register-level bounds; array reads/writes are charged
separately. The fixed13-entry Frodo CDF scan is unrolled. None of these costs
are measured CPython instruction counts. The bounds specify an elementary
implementation; they are deliberately less optimized than production kernels.

estimates.label: Native-message enumeration

assumptions.title: At most one eighth of honest messages fail to decode
assumptions.human: For the actual seeded scheme, require \(\Pr[D(F(m))\ne m]\le 1/8\). The ideal-noise correctness analysis supports this conservative threshold, but its transfer to fixed SHAKE remains a premise.
assumptions.technical: Assume the actual seeded key/message/salt distribution has message-decoding failure probability at most1/8. The local exact rational Chernoff/union certificate bounds the64 residuals E''+sum(S'E−E'S), with threshold4096, by2^-133 under independent finite-CDF noise. That stronger ideal-model statement motivates, but does not prove, the weaker actual-event bound used here. No literal independence of a long deterministic SHAKE expansion is claimed.

estimates.human: Try every 128-bit native message while keeping the observed public salt fixed; reproduce the full ciphertext and final shared key. The nearly flat ceiling comes from the real fixed message space. It is not evidence that lattice attacks are equally expensive.
estimates.technical:
### Why enumeration recovers the complete shared secret

Fix an honest key and any public encapsulation salt. Let F(x) be the deterministic
ciphertext produced by native input x and K(x) its derived key. Enumerate every
input and return K(x) for the first exact full-ciphertext match. This algorithm
does not receive a correctness oracle or the challenge target key.

Suppose an honest PKE decoder D fails to return x on at most a fraction delta of
uniform native inputs. The good inputs are injective under F: D(F(x)) cannot
equal two different x. A first-match attack can be wrong on at most all bad
inputs, plus one good input for each bad first representative. There are at most
as many such good inputs as bad inputs. Hence its key-recovery success is at
least 1-2*delta. The statement also holds after averaging over keys and salts.
It uses message recovery, not merely agreement of KEM outputs. No hash collision
resistance or random-oracle premise is needed for this combinatorial lemma.

This is a full-space, worst-case work budget that achieves at least 1/2 success;
it is not the minimum possible budget for 1/2 success. Early stopping only saves
work. Where every input decodes, success is exactly one in the mathematical
implementation. Operational faults are not a cryptanalytic assumption.

### Exact salted Frodo account
For n=328, q=32768 and nbar8, precompute all n public SHAKE128 rows and H(pk). For each of 2^128 messages use the observed 32-byte ciphertext salt. Expand 16n+64 noise values; a linear scan of the 13 CDF thresholds reproduces bisect_left exactly. Compute S'A and S'B with 8n²+64n modular multiply-adds. Encode, compare the entire ciphertext including its salt, and compute SHAKE128(ct||k,16). Native message search does not guess the public salt and does not truncate any seed. Final shared-key hashing is charged for every candidate, a conservative overhead.

### Memory layout and control conventions

Polynomial and matrix scalar slots and matrix row strides are padded to powers
of two. An indexed slot address is the concatenation of the public-width index
and a fixed intra-slot bit offset; bit transfers inside a scalar are unrolled.
The storage bound includes that padding. Loop/control allowances cover up to
eight counter increment/comparison pairs per compound step. Arithmetic
subroutines use the common register-level bounds; array reads/writes are charged
separately. The fixed13-entry Frodo CDF scan is unrolled. None of these costs
are measured CPython instruction counts. The bounds specify an elementary
implementation; they are deliberately less optimized than production kernels.

estimates.label: Native-message enumeration

assumptions.title: At most one eighth of honest messages fail to decode
assumptions.human: For the actual seeded scheme, require \(\Pr[D(F(m))\ne m]\le 1/8\). The ideal-noise correctness analysis supports this conservative threshold, but its transfer to fixed SHAKE remains a premise.
assumptions.technical: Assume the actual seeded key/message/salt distribution has message-decoding failure probability at most1/8. The local exact rational Chernoff/union certificate bounds the64 residuals E''+sum(S'E−E'S), with threshold4096, by2^-133 under independent finite-CDF noise. That stronger ideal-model statement motivates, but does not prove, the weaker actual-event bound used here. No literal independence of a long deterministic SHAKE expansion is claimed.

estimates.human: Try every 128-bit native message while keeping the observed public salt fixed; reproduce the full ciphertext and final shared key. The nearly flat ceiling comes from the real fixed message space. It is not evidence that lattice attacks are equally expensive.
estimates.technical:
### Why enumeration recovers the complete shared secret

Fix an honest key and any public encapsulation salt. Let F(x) be the deterministic
ciphertext produced by native input x and K(x) its derived key. Enumerate every
input and return K(x) for the first exact full-ciphertext match. This algorithm
does not receive a correctness oracle or the challenge target key.

Suppose an honest PKE decoder D fails to return x on at most a fraction delta of
uniform native inputs. The good inputs are injective under F: D(F(x)) cannot
equal two different x. A first-match attack can be wrong on at most all bad
inputs, plus one good input for each bad first representative. There are at most
as many such good inputs as bad inputs. Hence its key-recovery success is at
least 1-2*delta. The statement also holds after averaging over keys and salts.
It uses message recovery, not merely agreement of KEM outputs. No hash collision
resistance or random-oracle premise is needed for this combinatorial lemma.

This is a full-space, worst-case work budget that achieves at least 1/2 success;
it is not the minimum possible budget for 1/2 success. Early stopping only saves
work. Where every input decodes, success is exactly one in the mathematical
implementation. Operational faults are not a cryptanalytic assumption.

### Exact salted Frodo account
For n=464, q=32768 and nbar8, precompute all n public SHAKE128 rows and H(pk). For each of 2^128 messages use the observed 32-byte ciphertext salt. Expand 16n+64 noise values; a linear scan of the 13 CDF thresholds reproduces bisect_left exactly. Compute S'A and S'B with 8n²+64n modular multiply-adds. Encode, compare the entire ciphertext including its salt, and compute SHAKE128(ct||k,16). Native message search does not guess the public salt and does not truncate any seed. Final shared-key hashing is charged for every candidate, a conservative overhead.

### Memory layout and control conventions

Polynomial and matrix scalar slots and matrix row strides are padded to powers
of two. An indexed slot address is the concatenation of the public-width index
and a fixed intra-slot bit offset; bit transfers inside a scalar are unrolled.
The storage bound includes that padding. Loop/control allowances cover up to
eight counter increment/comparison pairs per compound step. Arithmetic
subroutines use the common register-level bounds; array reads/writes are charged
separately. The fixed13-entry Frodo CDF scan is unrolled. None of these costs
are measured CPython instruction counts. The bounds specify an elementary
implementation; they are deliberately less optimized than production kernels.

estimates.label: Native-message enumeration

assumptions.title: At most one eighth of honest messages fail to decode
assumptions.human: For the actual seeded scheme, require \(\Pr[D(F(m))\ne m]\le 1/8\). The ideal-noise correctness analysis supports this conservative threshold, but its transfer to fixed SHAKE remains a premise.
assumptions.technical: Assume the actual seeded key/message/salt distribution has message-decoding failure probability at most1/8. The local exact rational Chernoff/union certificate bounds the64 residuals E''+sum(S'E−E'S), with threshold4096, by2^-133 under independent finite-CDF noise. That stronger ideal-model statement motivates, but does not prove, the weaker actual-event bound used here. No literal independence of a long deterministic SHAKE expansion is claimed.

estimates.human: Try every 128-bit native message while keeping the observed public salt fixed; reproduce the full ciphertext and final shared key. The nearly flat ceiling comes from the real fixed message space. It is not evidence that lattice attacks are equally expensive.
estimates.technical:
### Why enumeration recovers the complete shared secret

Fix an honest key and any public encapsulation salt. Let F(x) be the deterministic
ciphertext produced by native input x and K(x) its derived key. Enumerate every
input and return K(x) for the first exact full-ciphertext match. This algorithm
does not receive a correctness oracle or the challenge target key.

Suppose an honest PKE decoder D fails to return x on at most a fraction delta of
uniform native inputs. The good inputs are injective under F: D(F(x)) cannot
equal two different x. A first-match attack can be wrong on at most all bad
inputs, plus one good input for each bad first representative. There are at most
as many such good inputs as bad inputs. Hence its key-recovery success is at
least 1-2*delta. The statement also holds after averaging over keys and salts.
It uses message recovery, not merely agreement of KEM outputs. No hash collision
resistance or random-oracle premise is needed for this combinatorial lemma.

This is a full-space, worst-case work budget that achieves at least 1/2 success;
it is not the minimum possible budget for 1/2 success. Early stopping only saves
work. Where every input decodes, success is exactly one in the mathematical
implementation. Operational faults are not a cryptanalytic assumption.

### Exact salted Frodo account
For n=600, q=32768 and nbar8, precompute all n public SHAKE128 rows and H(pk). For each of 2^128 messages use the observed 32-byte ciphertext salt. Expand 16n+64 noise values; a linear scan of the 13 CDF thresholds reproduces bisect_left exactly. Compute S'A and S'B with 8n²+64n modular multiply-adds. Encode, compare the entire ciphertext including its salt, and compute SHAKE128(ct||k,16). Native message search does not guess the public salt and does not truncate any seed. Final shared-key hashing is charged for every candidate, a conservative overhead.

### Memory layout and control conventions

Polynomial and matrix scalar slots and matrix row strides are padded to powers
of two. An indexed slot address is the concatenation of the public-width index
and a fixed intra-slot bit offset; bit transfers inside a scalar are unrolled.
The storage bound includes that padding. Loop/control allowances cover up to
eight counter increment/comparison pairs per compound step. Arithmetic
subroutines use the common register-level bounds; array reads/writes are charged
separately. The fixed13-entry Frodo CDF scan is unrolled. None of these costs
are measured CPython instruction counts. The bounds specify an elementary
implementation; they are deliberately less optimized than production kernels.

estimates.label: Fixed-weight input enumeration
estimates.human: Enumerate every allowed fixed-weight ternary encapsulation input, reproduce the rounded polynomial and confirmation hash, then derive the shared key. Perfect message recovery makes this complete search unambiguous. Lattice and hybrid attacks can be much faster than this baseline.

### Why enumeration recovers the complete shared secret

Fix an honest key and any public encapsulation salt. Let F(x) be the deterministic
ciphertext produced by native input x and K(x) its derived key. Enumerate every
input and return K(x) for the first exact full-ciphertext match. This algorithm
does not receive a correctness oracle or the challenge target key.

Suppose an honest PKE decoder D fails to return x on at most a fraction delta of
uniform native inputs. The good inputs are injective under F: D(F(x)) cannot
equal two different x. A first-match attack can be wrong on at most all bad
inputs, plus one good input for each bad first representative. There are at most
as many such good inputs as bad inputs. Hence its key-recovery success is at
least 1-2*delta. The statement also holds after averaging over keys and salts.
It uses message recovery, not merely agreement of KEM outputs. No hash collision
resistance or random-oracle premise is needed for this combinatorial lemma.

This is a full-space, worst-case work budget that achieves at least 1/2 success;
it is not the minimum possible budget for 1/2 success. Early stopping only saves
work. Where every input decodes, success is exactly one in the mathematical
implementation. Operational faults are not a cryptanalytic assumption.

For p=137,q=1237,w=77, enumerate all C(p,w)·2^w supports/signs without repetition. Decode h and cache Hash4(pk). Schoolbook multiplication computes h*r modulo(q,x^p−x−1), followed by the specified centered rounding and mixed-radix encoding. Each mixed-radix merge has inputs<2^14 and product<2^28; a28-bit account suffices. Hash3(smallencode(r)), Hash2(...||Hash4(pk)) and Hash1(...||ciphertext) use the pinned SHA512-prefix transform, with full hash cost counted despite truncation to32bytes. The certified q>=16w+1 bound and exact ring arithmetic give perfect native-r recovery, hence injectivity of the honest ciphertext map. No hash-collision premise is required.

Polynomial and matrix scalar slots and matrix row strides are padded to powers
of two. An indexed slot address is the concatenation of the public-width index
and a fixed intra-slot bit offset; bit transfers inside a scalar are unrolled.
The storage bound includes that padding. Loop/control allowances cover up to
eight counter increment/comparison pairs per compound step. Arithmetic
subroutines use the common register-level bounds; array reads/writes are charged
separately. The fixed13-entry Frodo CDF scan is unrolled. None of these costs

estimates.human: Enumerate every allowed fixed-weight ternary encapsulation input, reproduce the rounded polynomial and confirmation hash, then derive the shared key. Perfect message recovery makes this complete search unambiguous. Lattice and hybrid attacks can be much faster than this baseline.
estimates.technical:
### Why enumeration recovers the complete shared secret

Fix an honest key and any public encapsulation salt. Let F(x) be the deterministic
ciphertext produced by native input x and K(x) its derived key. Enumerate every
input and return K(x) for the first exact full-ciphertext match. This algorithm
does not receive a correctness oracle or the challenge target key.

Suppose an honest PKE decoder D fails to return x on at most a fraction delta of
uniform native inputs. The good inputs are injective under F: D(F(x)) cannot
equal two different x. A first-match attack can be wrong on at most all bad
inputs, plus one good input for each bad first representative. There are at most
as many such good inputs as bad inputs. Hence its key-recovery success is at
least 1-2*delta. The statement also holds after averaging over keys and salts.
It uses message recovery, not merely agreement of KEM outputs. No hash collision
resistance or random-oracle premise is needed for this combinatorial lemma.

This is a full-space, worst-case work budget that achieves at least 1/2 success;
it is not the minimum possible budget for 1/2 success. Early stopping only saves
work. Where every input decodes, success is exactly one in the mathematical
implementation. Operational faults are not a cryptanalytic assumption.

### Exact NTRU account
For p=613,q=1459,w=91, enumerate all C(p,w)·2^w supports/signs without repetition. Decode h and cache Hash4(pk). Schoolbook multiplication computes h*r modulo(q,x^p−x−1), followed by the specified centered rounding and mixed-radix encoding. Each mixed-radix merge has inputs<2^14 and product<2^28; a28-bit account suffices. Hash3(smallencode(r)), Hash2(...||Hash4(pk)) and Hash1(...||ciphertext) use the pinned SHA512-prefix transform, with full hash cost counted despite truncation to32bytes. The certified q>=16w+1 bound and exact ring arithmetic give perfect native-r recovery, hence injectivity of the honest ciphertext map. No hash-collision premise is required.

### Memory layout and control conventions

Polynomial and matrix scalar slots and matrix row strides are padded to powers
of two. An indexed slot address is the concatenation of the public-width index
and a fixed intra-slot bit offset; bit transfers inside a scalar are unrolled.
The storage bound includes that padding. Loop/control allowances cover up to
eight counter increment/comparison pairs per compound step. Arithmetic
subroutines use the common register-level bounds; array reads/writes are charged
separately. The fixed13-entry Frodo CDF scan is unrolled. None of these costs
are measured CPython instruction counts. The bounds specify an elementary
implementation; they are deliberately less optimized than production kernels.

assumptions.title: Almost every public key has a unique small secret
assumptions.human: Under the actual seeded key generator, at most one in 64 public keys has a different pair of weight-w secrets that explains the same public relation. An ideal random-multiplier calculation strongly motivates this premise, but does not prove it for fixed SHAKE.
assumptions.technical: The required concrete premise is Pr_actual[there exists another weight-(w,w) pair x',y' with s=x'+h*y']<=1/64. For an ideal h uniform and independent of x,y, primitive-prime n and fixed weight w<n/2 imply Pr[h(y+y')=x+x']<=2^-(n-1) for each alternative pair. Thus the ideal failure probability is <=binom(n,w)(binom(n,w)-1)2^-(n-1). This much smaller ideal bound is supporting rationale only. We do not assert a fixed SHAKE image of 256-bit seeds is literally uniform over n bits or transfer that tiny ideal bound without justification. The attack computes actual SHAKE and subtracts1/64, not the ideal-model probability, in its success claim.

estimates.human: Recover the small private vector from the public relation s=x+hy, then decode the ciphertext and derive its 32-byte secret. The displayed budget uses the cheaper of full support enumeration and a simple information-set attack, with the relevant assumptions shown for that choice. It includes decoding and hashing. This baseline omits faster specialized attacks and is not estimated best-known security.
estimates.technical:
## Attack specification: private support recovery then full KEM completion

The retained HQC2025 public relation is s=x+h*y in F2[X]/(X^n-1), where
wt(x)=wt(y)=w. One baseline enumerates every weight-w y, forms x=s+h*y,
and accepts when wt(x)=w. Another applies the explicitly bounded Prange
algorithm to H=[I_n|rot(h)], N=2n, r=n and target weight2w, then checks the
individual half weights. The smaller documented work budget is selected;
its premise set is selected with it. Prange uses the same rank-density
hypothesis and R=ceil(32 binom(2n,2w)/binom(n,2w)) accounting as the McEliece
note. Exhaustive enumeration needs no rank hypothesis and no uniform-secret
assumption: the true support is always visited.

For motivation, first analyze an ideal independent uniform public multiplier.
In that auxiliary model another weight-(w,w) solution has probability at most
epsilon=binom(n,w)(binom(n,w)-1)/2^(n-1). To see this, for y'!=y,
y+y' has even parity. Since n is primitive prime and2w<n-1, this nonzero
polynomial is not divisible by the irreducible degree-(n-1) factor of X^n-1.
Multiplication by it maps uniform h uniformly onto the even-parity subspace.
Each fixed x' therefore satisfies the alternative equation with probability
at most2^-(n-1). Apply a union bound; no independence of those alternatives
is needed. The bound is checked per profile and is below1/64. For the actual
fixed SHAKE implementation the visible premise is only that alternative-key
probability is at most1/64. This is an unproved event-level transfer claim;
the tiny ideal-model bound is not transplanted to the finite seeded output
space. The attack explicitly computes SHAKE and pays its cost.

Once y is recovered, compute v+u*y and truncate to the code length. For each
repeated RM(1,7) block, compare all256 affine words and choose nearest,
breaking ties by linear-mask order and then the constant bit. Decode the
shortened cyclic RS code using syndromes, Berlekamp-Massey, locator roots and
a GF256 Vandermonde solve for error values; recheck syndromes. Extract the
systematic16-byte message. The full secret is the first32 bytes of
SHA3-512(SHA3-256(pk||0x01)||message||salt||0x00).

The primitive-recovery success is at least1-1/64 for full support enumeration,
or at least21/32-1/64 for Prange. The existing October29 support proof bounds
the honest residual weight by B=2*w*wr+we. A repeated RM block can decode
incorrectly only after at least32*r errors, counting ties as potentially wrong;
RS(16+2*delta,16) corrects delta wrong symbols. Thus B<(delta+1)*32*r proves
zero honest decoding failure for every supported draw, without an ideal-XOF
or independent-noise premise. The actual tuple is checked against this strict
criterion; among the current66 profiles exactly stages1-4 satisfy it. See
docs/hqc-module-progression-review-20261029.txt and
docs/hqc-support-review-20261029.json. Otherwise subtract the actual honest
decoding-failure probability<=2^-128 using the explicit conditional premise.
No independence between correctness, rank and uniqueness events is assumed.

The budget charges SHAKE expansion, public-matrix construction (Prange only),
all finite trials/support candidates, cyclic multiplication, an explicit256-word
nearest-RM decoder, polynomial RS decoding and both final SHA3 evaluations.
GF256 multiplication uses eight shift/XOR/reduction rounds (<=1024 bit ops),
and inversion by x^254 costs<=16 multiplications. RS work is bounded by
4L^3+32L^2+512L+4096 field/control slots, each paying1024 plus the address/
transfer/control allowance; this covers the cubic error-value solve, all
syndrome evaluations, BM, root evaluation and initialization. The reference
Python kernel executes this path but its wall-clock runtime is not the unit.
The implementation deliberately overcounts rather than claiming optimized
native timings. Source parameters and byte formats are those of the exact
modeled-research-v3 adapter; the2026 HQC parameter changes are not imported.

These baselines do not represent the cheapest known HQC attacks. In particular,
quasi-cyclic improvements, modern ISD and public-message enumeration may be
cheaper. The conditional upper-bound curve should not be labelled a lower
bound on security or evidence that a NIST category is met.

For this tuple B=2*w*wr+we=6 < (delta+1)*32*r=64. The existing support proof therefore gives zero honest decoding failure, including deterministic ties, without an independent-noise or ideal-XOF premise. No correctness failure term is subtracted.

estimates.algorithm: Prange recovery of the quasi-cyclic private key

assumptions.title: Enough information sets remain invertible
assumptions.human: For at least seven eighths of honest targets, at least one eighth of the selected column sets that contain the true error support give an invertible matrix. This is a working hypothesis about the actual structured public matrices; it has not been established for every stage. The curve is conditional on it.
assumptions.technical: Write H as an r-by-N binary matrix and e for the actual weight-t target. With probability at least7/8 over the honest target draw, Pr_J[rank(H_J)=r | supp(e) subset J] >=1/8, where J is uniform among r-subsets. This is a per-instance density condition on a 7/8-measure good set, not an average success probability that can be amplified without justification. Fresh trials are independent conditional on H,e. Neither random-matrix heuristics nor toy checks prove this claim for binary Goppa or quasi-cyclic matrices.

assumptions.title: Almost every public key has a unique small secret
assumptions.human: Under the actual seeded key generator, at most one in 64 public keys has a different pair of weight-w secrets that explains the same public relation. An ideal random-multiplier calculation strongly motivates this premise, but does not prove it for fixed SHAKE.
assumptions.technical: The required concrete premise is Pr_actual[there exists another weight-(w,w) pair x',y' with s=x'+h*y']<=1/64. For an ideal h uniform and independent of x,y, primitive-prime n and fixed weight w<n/2 imply Pr[h(y+y')=x+x']<=2^-(n-1) for each alternative pair. Thus the ideal failure probability is <=binom(n,w)(binom(n,w)-1)2^-(n-1). This much smaller ideal bound is supporting rationale only. We do not assert a fixed SHAKE image of 256-bit seeds is literally uniform over n bits or transfer that tiny ideal bound without justification. The attack computes actual SHAKE and subtracts1/64, not the ideal-model probability, in its success claim.

assumptions.title: The stated decoding-failure bound applies to the actual scheme
assumptions.human: The scheme's conditional correctness analysis must bound actual honest decoding failure by 2^-128, including correlated ring errors and the chosen tie rule. Its surrogate-to-real-noise premise is still unproved for these research stages.
assumptions.technical: Use the retained per-profile conditional correctness certificate and its model-transfer premise to assert Pr[the concatenated nearest-RM/bounded-distance-RS decoder fails on an honest encapsulation]<=2^-128. The explicit attack decoder uses the same nearest-RM tie order (linear mask first, then constant) and the unique RS codeword within delta symbol errors. This transfer includes compatibility of those tie and decoding conventions. Subtract this failure probability by union bound; independence from rank or uniqueness events is not assumed.

estimates.human: Recover the small private vector from the public relation s=x+hy, then decode the ciphertext and derive its 32-byte secret. The displayed budget uses the cheaper of full support enumeration and a simple information-set attack, with the relevant assumptions shown for that choice. It includes decoding and hashing. This baseline omits faster specialized attacks and is not estimated best-known security.
estimates.technical:
## Attack specification: private support recovery then full KEM completion

The retained HQC2025 public relation is s=x+h*y in F2[X]/(X^n-1), where
wt(x)=wt(y)=w. One baseline enumerates every weight-w y, forms x=s+h*y,
and accepts when wt(x)=w. Another applies the explicitly bounded Prange
algorithm to H=[I_n|rot(h)], N=2n, r=n and target weight2w, then checks the
individual half weights. The smaller documented work budget is selected;
its premise set is selected with it. Prange uses the same rank-density
hypothesis and R=ceil(32 binom(2n,2w)/binom(n,2w)) accounting as the McEliece
note. Exhaustive enumeration needs no rank hypothesis and no uniform-secret
assumption: the true support is always visited.

For motivation, first analyze an ideal independent uniform public multiplier.
In that auxiliary model another weight-(w,w) solution has probability at most
epsilon=binom(n,w)(binom(n,w)-1)/2^(n-1). To see this, for y'!=y,
y+y' has even parity. Since n is primitive prime and2w<n-1, this nonzero
polynomial is not divisible by the irreducible degree-(n-1) factor of X^n-1.
Multiplication by it maps uniform h uniformly onto the even-parity subspace.
Each fixed x' therefore satisfies the alternative equation with probability
at most2^-(n-1). Apply a union bound; no independence of those alternatives
is needed. The bound is checked per profile and is below1/64. For the actual
fixed SHAKE implementation the visible premise is only that alternative-key
probability is at most1/64. This is an unproved event-level transfer claim;
the tiny ideal-model bound is not transplanted to the finite seeded output
space. The attack explicitly computes SHAKE and pays its cost.

Once y is recovered, compute v+u*y and truncate to the code length. For each
repeated RM(1,7) block, compare all256 affine words and choose nearest,
breaking ties by linear-mask order and then the constant bit. Decode the
shortened cyclic RS code using syndromes, Berlekamp-Massey, locator roots and
a GF256 Vandermonde solve for error values; recheck syndromes. Extract the
systematic16-byte message. The full secret is the first32 bytes of
SHA3-512(SHA3-256(pk||0x01)||message||salt||0x00).

The primitive-recovery success is at least1-1/64 for full support enumeration,
or at least21/32-1/64 for Prange. The existing October29 support proof bounds
the honest residual weight by B=2*w*wr+we. A repeated RM block can decode
incorrectly only after at least32*r errors, counting ties as potentially wrong;
RS(16+2*delta,16) corrects delta wrong symbols. Thus B<(delta+1)*32*r proves
zero honest decoding failure for every supported draw, without an ideal-XOF
or independent-noise premise. The actual tuple is checked against this strict
criterion; among the current66 profiles exactly stages1-4 satisfy it. See
docs/hqc-module-progression-review-20261029.txt and
docs/hqc-support-review-20261029.json. Otherwise subtract the actual honest
decoding-failure probability<=2^-128 using the explicit conditional premise.
No independence between correctness, rank and uniqueness events is assumed.

The budget charges SHAKE expansion, public-matrix construction (Prange only),
all finite trials/support candidates, cyclic multiplication, an explicit256-word
nearest-RM decoder, polynomial RS decoding and both final SHA3 evaluations.
GF256 multiplication uses eight shift/XOR/reduction rounds (<=1024 bit ops),
and inversion by x^254 costs<=16 multiplications. RS work is bounded by
4L^3+32L^2+512L+4096 field/control slots, each paying1024 plus the address/
transfer/control allowance; this covers the cubic error-value solve, all
syndrome evaluations, BM, root evaluation and initialization. The reference
Python kernel executes this path but its wall-clock runtime is not the unit.
The implementation deliberately overcounts rather than claiming optimized
native timings. Source parameters and byte formats are those of the exact
modeled-research-v3 adapter; the2026 HQC parameter changes are not imported.

These baselines do not represent the cheapest known HQC attacks. In particular,
quasi-cyclic improvements, modern ISD and public-message enumeration may be
cheaper. The conditional upper-bound curve should not be labelled a lower
bound on security or evidence that a NIST category is met.

For this tuple the deterministic support criterion is not established; subtract2^-128 under the stated actual honest-decoding premise.

assumptions.human: For at least seven eighths of honest targets, at least one eighth of the selected column sets that contain the true error support give an invertible matrix. This is a working hypothesis about the actual structured public matrices; it has not been established for every stage. The curve is conditional on it.
assumptions.technical: Write H as an r-by-N binary matrix and e for the actual weight-t target. With probability at least7/8 over the honest target draw, Pr_J[rank(H_J)=r | supp(e) subset J] >=1/8, where J is uniform among r-subsets. This is a per-instance density condition on a 7/8-measure good set, not an average success probability that can be amplified without justification. Fresh trials are independent conditional on H,e. Neither random-matrix heuristics nor toy checks prove this claim for binary Goppa or quasi-cyclic matrices.

assumptions.title: Almost every public key has a unique small secret
assumptions.human: Under the actual seeded key generator, at most one in 64 public keys has a different pair of weight-w secrets that explains the same public relation. An ideal random-multiplier calculation strongly motivates this premise, but does not prove it for fixed SHAKE.
assumptions.technical: The required concrete premise is Pr_actual[there exists another weight-(w,w) pair x',y' with s=x'+h*y']<=1/64. For an ideal h uniform and independent of x,y, primitive-prime n and fixed weight w<n/2 imply Pr[h(y+y')=x+x']<=2^-(n-1) for each alternative pair. Thus the ideal failure probability is <=binom(n,w)(binom(n,w)-1)2^-(n-1). This much smaller ideal bound is supporting rationale only. We do not assert a fixed SHAKE image of 256-bit seeds is literally uniform over n bits or transfer that tiny ideal bound without justification. The attack computes actual SHAKE and subtracts1/64, not the ideal-model probability, in its success claim.

assumptions.title: The stated decoding-failure bound applies to the actual scheme
assumptions.human: The scheme's conditional correctness analysis must bound actual honest decoding failure by 2^-128, including correlated ring errors and the chosen tie rule. Its surrogate-to-real-noise premise is still unproved for these research stages.
assumptions.technical: Use the retained per-profile conditional correctness certificate and its model-transfer premise to assert Pr[the concatenated nearest-RM/bounded-distance-RS decoder fails on an honest encapsulation]<=2^-128. The explicit attack decoder uses the same nearest-RM tie order (linear mask first, then constant) and the unique RS codeword within delta symbol errors. This transfer includes compatibility of those tie and decoding conventions. Subtract this failure probability by union bound; independence from rank or uniqueness events is not assumed.

estimates.human: Recover the small private vector from the public relation s=x+hy, then decode the ciphertext and derive its 32-byte secret. The displayed budget uses the cheaper of full support enumeration and a simple information-set attack, with the relevant assumptions shown for that choice. It includes decoding and hashing. This baseline omits faster specialized attacks and is not estimated best-known security.
estimates.technical:
## Attack specification: private support recovery then full KEM completion

The retained HQC2025 public relation is s=x+h*y in F2[X]/(X^n-1), where
wt(x)=wt(y)=w. One baseline enumerates every weight-w y, forms x=s+h*y,
and accepts when wt(x)=w. Another applies the explicitly bounded Prange
algorithm to H=[I_n|rot(h)], N=2n, r=n and target weight2w, then checks the
individual half weights. The smaller documented work budget is selected;
its premise set is selected with it. Prange uses the same rank-density
hypothesis and R=ceil(32 binom(2n,2w)/binom(n,2w)) accounting as the McEliece
note. Exhaustive enumeration needs no rank hypothesis and no uniform-secret
assumption: the true support is always visited.

For motivation, first analyze an ideal independent uniform public multiplier.
In that auxiliary model another weight-(w,w) solution has probability at most
epsilon=binom(n,w)(binom(n,w)-1)/2^(n-1). To see this, for y'!=y,
y+y' has even parity. Since n is primitive prime and2w<n-1, this nonzero
polynomial is not divisible by the irreducible degree-(n-1) factor of X^n-1.
Multiplication by it maps uniform h uniformly onto the even-parity subspace.
Each fixed x' therefore satisfies the alternative equation with probability
at most2^-(n-1). Apply a union bound; no independence of those alternatives
is needed. The bound is checked per profile and is below1/64. For the actual
fixed SHAKE implementation the visible premise is only that alternative-key
probability is at most1/64. This is an unproved event-level transfer claim;
the tiny ideal-model bound is not transplanted to the finite seeded output
space. The attack explicitly computes SHAKE and pays its cost.

Once y is recovered, compute v+u*y and truncate to the code length. For each
repeated RM(1,7) block, compare all256 affine words and choose nearest,
breaking ties by linear-mask order and then the constant bit. Decode the
shortened cyclic RS code using syndromes, Berlekamp-Massey, locator roots and
a GF256 Vandermonde solve for error values; recheck syndromes. Extract the
systematic16-byte message. The full secret is the first32 bytes of
SHA3-512(SHA3-256(pk||0x01)||message||salt||0x00).

The primitive-recovery success is at least1-1/64 for full support enumeration,
or at least21/32-1/64 for Prange. The existing October29 support proof bounds
the honest residual weight by B=2*w*wr+we. A repeated RM block can decode
incorrectly only after at least32*r errors, counting ties as potentially wrong;
RS(16+2*delta,16) corrects delta wrong symbols. Thus B<(delta+1)*32*r proves
zero honest decoding failure for every supported draw, without an ideal-XOF
or independent-noise premise. The actual tuple is checked against this strict
criterion; among the current66 profiles exactly stages1-4 satisfy it. See
docs/hqc-module-progression-review-20261029.txt and
docs/hqc-support-review-20261029.json. Otherwise subtract the actual honest
decoding-failure probability<=2^-128 using the explicit conditional premise.
No independence between correctness, rank and uniqueness events is assumed.

The budget charges SHAKE expansion, public-matrix construction (Prange only),
all finite trials/support candidates, cyclic multiplication, an explicit256-word
nearest-RM decoder, polynomial RS decoding and both final SHA3 evaluations.
GF256 multiplication uses eight shift/XOR/reduction rounds (<=1024 bit ops),
and inversion by x^254 costs<=16 multiplications. RS work is bounded by
4L^3+32L^2+512L+4096 field/control slots, each paying1024 plus the address/
transfer/control allowance; this covers the cubic error-value solve, all
syndrome evaluations, BM, root evaluation and initialization. The reference
Python kernel executes this path but its wall-clock runtime is not the unit.
The implementation deliberately overcounts rather than claiming optimized
native timings. Source parameters and byte formats are those of the exact
modeled-research-v3 adapter; the2026 HQC parameter changes are not imported.

These baselines do not represent the cheapest known HQC attacks. In particular,
quasi-cyclic improvements, modern ISD and public-message enumeration may be
cheaper. The conditional upper-bound curve should not be labelled a lower
bound on security or evidence that a NIST category is met.

For this tuple the deterministic support criterion is not established; subtract2^-128 under the stated actual honest-decoding premise.

This is a working hypothesis about the actual structured public matrices; it has not been established for every stage. The curve is conditional on it.
assumptions.technical: Write H as an r-by-N binary matrix and e for the actual weight-t target. With probability at least7/8 over the honest target draw, Pr_J[rank(H_J)=r | supp(e) subset J] >=1/8, where J is uniform among r-subsets. This is a per-instance density condition on a 7/8-measure good set, not an average success probability that can be amplified without justification. Fresh trials are independent conditional on H,e. Neither random-matrix heuristics nor toy checks prove this claim for binary Goppa or quasi-cyclic matrices.

assumptions.title: Almost every public key has a unique small secret
assumptions.human: Under the actual seeded key generator, at most one in 64 public keys has a different pair of weight-w secrets that explains the same public relation. An ideal random-multiplier calculation strongly motivates this premise, but does not prove it for fixed SHAKE.
assumptions.technical: The required concrete premise is Pr_actual[there exists another weight-(w,w) pair x',y' with s=x'+h*y']<=1/64. For an ideal h uniform and independent of x,y, primitive-prime n and fixed weight w<n/2 imply Pr[h(y+y')=x+x']<=2^-(n-1) for each alternative pair. Thus the ideal failure probability is <=binom(n,w)(binom(n,w)-1)2^-(n-1). This much smaller ideal bound is supporting rationale only. We do not assert a fixed SHAKE image of 256-bit seeds is literally uniform over n bits or transfer that tiny ideal bound without justification. The attack computes actual SHAKE and subtracts1/64, not the ideal-model probability, in its success claim.

assumptions.title: The stated decoding-failure bound applies to the actual scheme
assumptions.human: The scheme's conditional correctness analysis must bound actual honest decoding failure by 2^-128, including correlated ring errors and the chosen tie rule. Its surrogate-to-real-noise premise is still unproved for these research stages.
assumptions.technical: Use the retained per-profile conditional correctness certificate and its model-transfer premise to assert Pr[the concatenated nearest-RM/bounded-distance-RS decoder fails on an honest encapsulation]<=2^-128. The explicit attack decoder uses the same nearest-RM tie order (linear mask first, then constant) and the unique RS codeword within delta symbol errors. This transfer includes compatibility of those tie and decoding conventions. Subtract this failure probability by union bound; independence from rank or uniqueness events is not assumed.

estimates.human: Recover the small private vector from the public relation s=x+hy, then decode the ciphertext and derive its 32-byte secret. The displayed budget uses the cheaper of full support enumeration and a simple information-set attack, with the relevant assumptions shown for that choice. It includes decoding and hashing. This baseline omits faster specialized attacks and is not estimated best-known security.
estimates.technical:
## Attack specification: private support recovery then full KEM completion

The retained HQC2025 public relation is s=x+h*y in F2[X]/(X^n-1), where
wt(x)=wt(y)=w. One baseline enumerates every weight-w y, forms x=s+h*y,
and accepts when wt(x)=w. Another applies the explicitly bounded Prange
algorithm to H=[I_n|rot(h)], N=2n, r=n and target weight2w, then checks the
individual half weights. The smaller documented work budget is selected;
its premise set is selected with it. Prange uses the same rank-density
hypothesis and R=ceil(32 binom(2n,2w)/binom(n,2w)) accounting as the McEliece
note. Exhaustive enumeration needs no rank hypothesis and no uniform-secret
assumption: the true support is always visited.

For motivation, first analyze an ideal independent uniform public multiplier.
In that auxiliary model another weight-(w,w) solution has probability at most
epsilon=binom(n,w)(binom(n,w)-1)/2^(n-1). To see this, for y'!=y,
y+y' has even parity. Since n is primitive prime and2w<n-1, this nonzero
polynomial is not divisible by the irreducible degree-(n-1) factor of X^n-1.
Multiplication by it maps uniform h uniformly onto the even-parity subspace.
Each fixed x' therefore satisfies the alternative equation with probability
at most2^-(n-1). Apply a union bound; no independence of those alternatives
is needed. The bound is checked per profile and is below1/64. For the actual
fixed SHAKE implementation the visible premise is only that alternative-key
probability is at most1/64. This is an unproved event-level transfer claim;
the tiny ideal-model bound is not transplanted to the finite seeded output
space. The attack explicitly computes SHAKE and pays its cost.

Once y is recovered, compute v+u*y and truncate to the code length. For each
repeated RM(1,7) block, compare all256 affine words and choose nearest,
breaking ties by linear-mask order and then the constant bit. Decode the
shortened cyclic RS code using syndromes, Berlekamp-Massey, locator roots and
a GF256 Vandermonde solve for error values; recheck syndromes. Extract the
systematic16-byte message. The full secret is the first32 bytes of
SHA3-512(SHA3-256(pk||0x01)||message||salt||0x00).

The primitive-recovery success is at least1-1/64 for full support enumeration,
or at least21/32-1/64 for Prange. The existing October29 support proof bounds
the honest residual weight by B=2*w*wr+we. A repeated RM block can decode
incorrectly only after at least32*r errors, counting ties as potentially wrong;
RS(16+2*delta,16) corrects delta wrong symbols. Thus B<(delta+1)*32*r proves
zero honest decoding failure for every supported draw, without an ideal-XOF
or independent-noise premise. The actual tuple is checked against this strict
criterion; among the current66 profiles exactly stages1-4 satisfy it. See
docs/hqc-module-progression-review-20261029.txt and
docs/hqc-support-review-20261029.json. Otherwise subtract the actual honest
decoding-failure probability<=2^-128 using the explicit conditional premise.
No independence between correctness, rank and uniqueness events is assumed.

The budget charges SHAKE expansion, public-matrix construction (Prange only),
all finite trials/support candidates, cyclic multiplication, an explicit256-word
nearest-RM decoder, polynomial RS decoding and both final SHA3 evaluations.
GF256 multiplication uses eight shift/XOR/reduction rounds (<=1024 bit ops),
and inversion by x^254 costs<=16 multiplications. RS work is bounded by
4L^3+32L^2+512L+4096 field/control slots, each paying1024 plus the address/
transfer/control allowance; this covers the cubic error-value solve, all
syndrome evaluations, BM, root evaluation and initialization. The reference
Python kernel executes this path but its wall-clock runtime is not the unit.
The implementation deliberately overcounts rather than claiming optimized
native timings. Source parameters and byte formats are those of the exact
modeled-research-v3 adapter; the2026 HQC parameter changes are not imported.

These baselines do not represent the cheapest known HQC attacks. In particular,
quasi-cyclic improvements, modern ISD and public-message enumeration may be
cheaper. The conditional upper-bound curve should not be labelled a lower
bound on security or evidence that a NIST category is met.

For this tuple the deterministic support criterion is not established; subtract2^-128 under the stated actual honest-decoding premise.

This is a working hypothesis about the actual structured public matrices; it has not been established for every stage. The curve is conditional on it.
assumptions.technical: Write H as an r-by-N binary matrix and e for the actual weight-t target. With probability at least7/8 over the honest target draw, Pr_J[rank(H_J)=r | supp(e) subset J] >=1/8, where J is uniform among r-subsets. This is a per-instance density condition on a 7/8-measure good set, not an average success probability that can be amplified without justification. Fresh trials are independent conditional on H,e. Neither random-matrix heuristics nor toy checks prove this claim for binary Goppa or quasi-cyclic matrices.

assumptions.title: Almost every public key has a unique small secret
assumptions.human: Under the actual seeded key generator, at most one in 64 public keys has a different pair of weight-w secrets that explains the same public relation. An ideal random-multiplier calculation strongly motivates this premise, but does not prove it for fixed SHAKE.
assumptions.technical: The required concrete premise is Pr_actual[there exists another weight-(w,w) pair x',y' with s=x'+h*y']<=1/64. For an ideal h uniform and independent of x,y, primitive-prime n and fixed weight w<n/2 imply Pr[h(y+y')=x+x']<=2^-(n-1) for each alternative pair. Thus the ideal failure probability is <=binom(n,w)(binom(n,w)-1)2^-(n-1). This much smaller ideal bound is supporting rationale only. We do not assert a fixed SHAKE image of 256-bit seeds is literally uniform over n bits or transfer that tiny ideal bound without justification. The attack computes actual SHAKE and subtracts1/64, not the ideal-model probability, in its success claim.

assumptions.title: The stated decoding-failure bound applies to the actual scheme
assumptions.human: The scheme's conditional correctness analysis must bound actual honest decoding failure by 2^-128, including correlated ring errors and the chosen tie rule. Its surrogate-to-real-noise premise is still unproved for these research stages.
assumptions.technical: Use the retained per-profile conditional correctness certificate and its model-transfer premise to assert Pr[the concatenated nearest-RM/bounded-distance-RS decoder fails on an honest encapsulation]<=2^-128. The explicit attack decoder uses the same nearest-RM tie order (linear mask first, then constant) and the unique RS codeword within delta symbol errors. This transfer includes compatibility of those tie and decoding conventions. Subtract this failure probability by union bound; independence from rank or uniqueness events is not assumed.

estimates.human: Recover the small private vector from the public relation s=x+hy, then decode the ciphertext and derive its 32-byte secret. The displayed budget uses the cheaper of full support enumeration and a simple information-set attack, with the relevant assumptions shown for that choice. It includes decoding and hashing. This baseline omits faster specialized attacks and is not estimated best-known security.
estimates.technical:
## Attack specification: private support recovery then full KEM completion

The retained HQC2025 public relation is s=x+h*y in F2[X]/(X^n-1), where
wt(x)=wt(y)=w. One baseline enumerates every weight-w y, forms x=s+h*y,
and accepts when wt(x)=w. Another applies the explicitly bounded Prange
algorithm to H=[I_n|rot(h)], N=2n, r=n and target weight2w, then checks the
individual half weights. The smaller documented work budget is selected;
its premise set is selected with it. Prange uses the same rank-density
hypothesis and R=ceil(32 binom(2n,2w)/binom(n,2w)) accounting as the McEliece
note. Exhaustive enumeration needs no rank hypothesis and no uniform-secret
assumption: the true support is always visited.

For motivation, first analyze an ideal independent uniform public multiplier.
In that auxiliary model another weight-(w,w) solution has probability at most
epsilon=binom(n,w)(binom(n,w)-1)/2^(n-1). To see this, for y'!=y,
y+y' has even parity. Since n is primitive prime and2w<n-1, this nonzero
polynomial is not divisible by the irreducible degree-(n-1) factor of X^n-1.
Multiplication by it maps uniform h uniformly onto the even-parity subspace.
Each fixed x' therefore satisfies the alternative equation with probability
at most2^-(n-1). Apply a union bound; no independence of those alternatives
is needed. The bound is checked per profile and is below1/64. For the actual
fixed SHAKE implementation the visible premise is only that alternative-key
probability is at most1/64. This is an unproved event-level transfer claim;
the tiny ideal-model bound is not transplanted to the finite seeded output
space. The attack explicitly computes SHAKE and pays its cost.

Once y is recovered, compute v+u*y and truncate to the code length. For each
repeated RM(1,7) block, compare all256 affine words and choose nearest,
breaking ties by linear-mask order and then the constant bit. Decode the
shortened cyclic RS code using syndromes, Berlekamp-Massey, locator roots and
a GF256 Vandermonde solve for error values; recheck syndromes. Extract the
systematic16-byte message. The full secret is the first32 bytes of
SHA3-512(SHA3-256(pk||0x01)||message||salt||0x00).

The primitive-recovery success is at least1-1/64 for full support enumeration,
or at least21/32-1/64 for Prange. The existing October29 support proof bounds
the honest residual weight by B=2*w*wr+we. A repeated RM block can decode
incorrectly only after at least32*r errors, counting ties as potentially wrong;
RS(16+2*delta,16) corrects delta wrong symbols. Thus B<(delta+1)*32*r proves
zero honest decoding failure for every supported draw, without an ideal-XOF
or independent-noise premise. The actual tuple is checked against this strict
criterion; among the current66 profiles exactly stages1-4 satisfy it. See
docs/hqc-module-progression-review-20261029.txt and
docs/hqc-support-review-20261029.json. Otherwise subtract the actual honest
decoding-failure probability<=2^-128 using the explicit conditional premise.
No independence between correctness, rank and uniqueness events is assumed.

The budget charges SHAKE expansion, public-matrix construction (Prange only),
all finite trials/support candidates, cyclic multiplication, an explicit256-word
nearest-RM decoder, polynomial RS decoding and both final SHA3 evaluations.
GF256 multiplication uses eight shift/XOR/reduction rounds (<=1024 bit ops),
and inversion by x^254 costs<=16 multiplications. RS work is bounded by
4L^3+32L^2+512L+4096 field/control slots, each paying1024 plus the address/
transfer/control allowance; this covers the cubic error-value solve, all
syndrome evaluations, BM, root evaluation and initialization. The reference
Python kernel executes this path but its wall-clock runtime is not the unit.
The implementation deliberately overcounts rather than claiming optimized
native timings. Source parameters and byte formats are those of the exact
modeled-research-v3 adapter; the2026 HQC parameter changes are not imported.

These baselines do not represent the cheapest known HQC attacks. In particular,
quasi-cyclic improvements, modern ISD and public-message enumeration may be
cheaper. The conditional upper-bound curve should not be labelled a lower
bound on security or evidence that a NIST category is met.

For this tuple the deterministic support criterion is not established; subtract2^-128 under the stated actual honest-decoding premise.

This is a working hypothesis about the actual structured public matrices; it has not been established for every stage. The curve is conditional on it.
assumptions.technical: Write H as an r-by-N binary matrix and e for the actual weight-t target. With probability at least7/8 over the honest target draw, Pr_J[rank(H_J)=r | supp(e) subset J] >=1/8, where J is uniform among r-subsets. This is a per-instance density condition on a 7/8-measure good set, not an average success probability that can be amplified without justification. Fresh trials are independent conditional on H,e. Neither random-matrix heuristics nor toy checks prove this claim for binary Goppa or quasi-cyclic matrices.

assumptions.title: Almost every public key has a unique small secret
assumptions.human: Under the actual seeded key generator, at most one in 64 public keys has a different pair of weight-w secrets that explains the same public relation. An ideal random-multiplier calculation strongly motivates this premise, but does not prove it for fixed SHAKE.
assumptions.technical: The required concrete premise is Pr_actual[there exists another weight-(w,w) pair x',y' with s=x'+h*y']<=1/64. For an ideal h uniform and independent of x,y, primitive-prime n and fixed weight w<n/2 imply Pr[h(y+y')=x+x']<=2^-(n-1) for each alternative pair. Thus the ideal failure probability is <=binom(n,w)(binom(n,w)-1)2^-(n-1). This much smaller ideal bound is supporting rationale only. We do not assert a fixed SHAKE image of 256-bit seeds is literally uniform over n bits or transfer that tiny ideal bound without justification. The attack computes actual SHAKE and subtracts1/64, not the ideal-model probability, in its success claim.

assumptions.title: The stated decoding-failure bound applies to the actual scheme
assumptions.human: The scheme's conditional correctness analysis must bound actual honest decoding failure by 2^-128, including correlated ring errors and the chosen tie rule. Its surrogate-to-real-noise premise is still unproved for these research stages.
assumptions.technical: Use the retained per-profile conditional correctness certificate and its model-transfer premise to assert Pr[the concatenated nearest-RM/bounded-distance-RS decoder fails on an honest encapsulation]<=2^-128. The explicit attack decoder uses the same nearest-RM tie order (linear mask first, then constant) and the unique RS codeword within delta symbol errors. This transfer includes compatibility of those tie and decoding conventions. Subtract this failure probability by union bound; independence from rank or uniqueness events is not assumed.

estimates.human: Recover the small private vector from the public relation s=x+hy, then decode the ciphertext and derive its 32-byte secret. The displayed budget uses the cheaper of full support enumeration and a simple information-set attack, with the relevant assumptions shown for that choice. It includes decoding and hashing. This baseline omits faster specialized attacks and is not estimated best-known security.
estimates.technical:
## Attack specification: private support recovery then full KEM completion

The retained HQC2025 public relation is s=x+h*y in F2[X]/(X^n-1), where
wt(x)=wt(y)=w. One baseline enumerates every weight-w y, forms x=s+h*y,
and accepts when wt(x)=w. Another applies the explicitly bounded Prange
algorithm to H=[I_n|rot(h)], N=2n, r=n and target weight2w, then checks the
individual half weights. The smaller documented work budget is selected;
its premise set is selected with it. Prange uses the same rank-density
hypothesis and R=ceil(32 binom(2n,2w)/binom(n,2w)) accounting as the McEliece
note. Exhaustive enumeration needs no rank hypothesis and no uniform-secret
assumption: the true support is always visited.

For motivation, first analyze an ideal independent uniform public multiplier.
In that auxiliary model another weight-(w,w) solution has probability at most
epsilon=binom(n,w)(binom(n,w)-1)/2^(n-1). To see this, for y'!=y,
y+y' has even parity. Since n is primitive prime and2w<n-1, this nonzero
polynomial is not divisible by the irreducible degree-(n-1) factor of X^n-1.
Multiplication by it maps uniform h uniformly onto the even-parity subspace.
Each fixed x' therefore satisfies the alternative equation with probability
at most2^-(n-1). Apply a union bound; no independence of those alternatives
is needed. The bound is checked per profile and is below1/64. For the actual
fixed SHAKE implementation the visible premise is only that alternative-key
probability is at most1/64. This is an unproved event-level transfer claim;
the tiny ideal-model bound is not transplanted to the finite seeded output
space. The attack explicitly computes SHAKE and pays its cost.

Once y is recovered, compute v+u*y and truncate to the code length. For each
repeated RM(1,7) block, compare all256 affine words and choose nearest,
breaking ties by linear-mask order and then the constant bit. Decode the
shortened cyclic RS code using syndromes, Berlekamp-Massey, locator roots and
a GF256 Vandermonde solve for error values; recheck syndromes. Extract the
systematic16-byte message. The full secret is the first32 bytes of
SHA3-512(SHA3-256(pk||0x01)||message||salt||0x00).

The primitive-recovery success is at least1-1/64 for full support enumeration,
or at least21/32-1/64 for Prange. The existing October29 support proof bounds
the honest residual weight by B=2*w*wr+we. A repeated RM block can decode
incorrectly only after at least32*r errors, counting ties as potentially wrong;
RS(16+2*delta,16) corrects delta wrong symbols. Thus B<(delta+1)*32*r proves
zero honest decoding failure for every supported draw, without an ideal-XOF
or independent-noise premise. The actual tuple is checked against this strict
criterion; among the current66 profiles exactly stages1-4 satisfy it. See
docs/hqc-module-progression-review-20261029.txt and
docs/hqc-support-review-20261029.json. Otherwise subtract the actual honest
decoding-failure probability<=2^-128 using the explicit conditional premise.
No independence between correctness, rank and uniqueness events is assumed.

The budget charges SHAKE expansion, public-matrix construction (Prange only),
all finite trials/support candidates, cyclic multiplication, an explicit256-word
nearest-RM decoder, polynomial RS decoding and both final SHA3 evaluations.
GF256 multiplication uses eight shift/XOR/reduction rounds (<=1024 bit ops),
and inversion by x^254 costs<=16 multiplications. RS work is bounded by
4L^3+32L^2+512L+4096 field/control slots, each paying1024 plus the address/
transfer/control allowance; this covers the cubic error-value solve, all
syndrome evaluations, BM, root evaluation and initialization. The reference
Python kernel executes this path but its wall-clock runtime is not the unit.
The implementation deliberately overcounts rather than claiming optimized
native timings. Source parameters and byte formats are those of the exact
modeled-research-v3 adapter; the2026 HQC parameter changes are not imported.

These baselines do not represent the cheapest known HQC attacks. In particular,
quasi-cyclic improvements, modern ISD and public-message enumeration may be
cheaper. The conditional upper-bound curve should not be labelled a lower
bound on security or evidence that a NIST category is met.

For this tuple the deterministic support criterion is not established; subtract2^-128 under the stated actual honest-decoding premise.
